Theme

Latin word

mediocris

mediocris, mediocre

adjective, third declension

average, middling, ordinary; mediocre; medium, middling, of moderate size

In this lexicon

  • average

    the recommended word · classical · Mart. 1.16.1: sunt quaedam mediocria; Cic. Brut. 136: ōrātōrēs mediocrēs (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. normal, ordinary, average

  • medium

    the recommended word · classical · Caes. BC 3.46.1: mediocrī lātitūdine fossam; Caes. BG 5.44.6: mediocrī spatiō relictō

  • nōn mediocris, nōn mediocre: significant

    classical

Notes

  1. 1mediocris: short o (Lewis & Short mediō̆cris, “ō usually; rarely ŏ”). De Vaan 424, s.v. ocris, prints mediocris without a macron and derives it from ocris, “rugged mountain” (PIE *h₂ok-r-i-): “orig. ‘situated at the middle, half-way of the top’”. In verse the vowel stands before cr, so the syllable can be heavy by position and the metre cannot show a long vowel (Hor. AP 370, 372).
